capabilities.oldImplementation: Custom Electron app name, dev.dsh.desktop.custom, isolated userData and desktop-custom profile, startup branding, and independent single-instance ownership.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: DSH_DESKTOP_APP_ID configures appId, but productName remains hard-coded, Desktop profile remains desktop, and startup/update identity was redesigned.

capabilities.capability: macOS arm64 package and safe daily install
capabilities.oldImplementation: Custom package/install scripts staged the bundled Node Host, signed the app, verified native modules, and installed beside official Desktop.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: A signed primary-runtime tree now bundles Node, Python, pnpm, payload digests, updater policy, and qualification stages.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Agent Run State projected session/run/attempt identity and terminal-safe phases from durable and transient sources.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: Upstream has turn/step lifecycle, LlmAttemptId, transient assistant stream, and durable retry events, but no DS Harness RunId projection.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Replaceable MLX/GGUF observers, prefill activity, independent process/model/generation health, and attribution confidence.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: No equivalent backend health or prefill observer was found.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Classified resource limits, worker crashes, cancellation, and secondary stream failures without replacing the root cause.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: LlmFailure now carries provider-neutral code/status/requestId facts but does not implement DS Harness backend-root-cause precedence.
validation: unknown errors do not become fatal

capabilities.oldImplementation: Fatal-aware bounded retries, cancellation acknowledgement, and no retry after terminal/fatal states.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: llm-retry provides durable same-turn retries and backoff, but normal mode defaults to five retries and its generic retryable classes do not encode DS Harness fatal backend evidence.

capabilities.capability: Task checkpoint, result manifest, and pending-only resume
capabilities.oldImplementation: Custom durable TaskCheckpoint/Result Manifest tracked objective, steps, outputs, failures, and resume eligibility.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: session-checkpoint-policy now flushes before model requests, side-effecting tools, and next steps; repair distinguishes TOOL_NOT_STARTED and TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, but there is no domain TaskCheckpoint/Result Manifest.

capabilities.capability: Crash durability and generic session resume foundation
capabilities.oldImplementation: Custom hooks forced durable boundaries and repaired interrupted runs.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: Native session-checkpoint-policy, resume registry, interrupted turn closure, lease verification, and repair semantics now provide the generic foundation.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Request-scoped xhigh-first classification, high to xhigh, off to none, benchmark lock, and auxiliary compaction scope isolation.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: llm-pi-ai supports request-level reasoningEffort, model-advertised effort values, strict unsupported errors, and request override, but does not encode the audited IQ3_S policy.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Pressure/eligibility separation, low then medium compaction, deterministic task-fact validation, atomic apply, and main-reasoning isolation.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: compaction-basic now provides token-meter thresholds, automatic/manual/overflow triggers, atomic brackets, shrink validation, cache-prefix reuse, image offload, and tool-result pruning.

capabilities.oldImplementation: Custom summary/key-line/reference retention reduced long-lived tool output.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: Native compaction tool-result pruner and image offload cover the generic surface reduction mechanism.

capabilities.capability: Run Details diagnostics and idle closure
capabilities.oldImplementation: Read-only diagnostics remote plus RunStatusDock displayed run/backend/context facts and returned run=null when idle.
capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: Client modules, generated catalogs, scoped slots, and ui-dockkit replace the old renderer surface; runtime invariants do not provide Run State UI.
validation: idle run=null occupies no composer space

capabilities.capability: Shared settings/sessions with isolated Electron state/profile

capabilities.upstreamEquivalent: Desktop and Host still default to desktop, while profile resolution and session v0-to-v3 migrations, generations, and leases are substantially newer.

requiredNewCustomSurface.requirement: Minimal product identity/profile/userData/branding configuration compatible with the new Desktop release pipeline.
Explicit desktop-custom isolation and fixture-only migration qualification.
A current package-set/Cordis composition containing only retained DS Harness capabilities.
RunId projection, backend observers, health/error precedence, and read-only diagnostics transport.
Bounded fatal-aware retry/cancel policy integrated once with upstream llm-retry.
TaskCheckpoint/Result Manifest v3 events, projections, guards, and pending-only resume.
IQ3_S capability mapping and xhigh-first request policy on upstream reasoningEffort.
Thin task-aware eligibility, reasoning scope, and deterministic validation around upstream compaction.
Run Details rebuilt for current remote/module/scoped-slot/dockkit contracts.
Phase 8B tooling ported after product contracts stabilize, without joining runtime composition.

seams.oldContract: Custom appId, productName, desktop-custom profile, isolated userData, startup title, and single-instance identity.
seams.newContract: appId is environment-resolved; productName and Desktop profile are fixed upstream; mandatory-update identity and startup shell are new.
seams.breakage: The old patch locations and startup renderer contract no longer map one-to-one.
seams.migration: Create a reviewed upstream-style product flavor seam before any candidate launch.

seams.oldContract: Custom scripts staged a Node Host/runtime descriptor and signed one macOS app.
seams.newContract: Primary runtime bundles pinned Node/Python/pnpm with payload hashes, update qualification, signing, and mandatory policy metadata.
seams.breakage: Old package/install scripts would bypass the new runtime and release closure.
seams.migration: Extend current packaging inputs; do not replay the old staging implementation.

seams.oldContract: desktop-custom-composition patched the then-current base/web Cordis graph.
seams.newContract: The package/module graph and generated catalogs have expanded and changed ownership.
seams.breakage: Old patch entries can reference removed packages or duplicate new native services.
seams.migration: Rebuild a minimal composition from the current package graph after identity/data gates.

seams.oldContract: Custom client packages were loaded through the old export/slot conventions.
seams.newContract: Generated client catalogs, module packages, scoped slots, factory slots, and dockkit drive loading.
seams.breakage: Old package exports and renderer entry assumptions are not valid.
seams.migration: Create current-format exports and generated-catalog entries; keep transport read-only.

seams.oldContract: desktop-custom isolated profile/userData while approved settings and sessions were shared.
seams.newContract: Desktop and Host default to desktop; profile resolution, primary runtime installation, and automatic session migrations are new.
seams.breakage: An unqualified launch could use the official profile or migrate shared stores under unreviewed assumptions.
seams.migration: Implement and test explicit paths against copied fixtures before any real profile access.

seams.oldContract: Run projection consumed older agent/session/tool/retry events with custom attempt correlation.
seams.newContract: Turn/step lifecycle, LlmAttemptId, compact assistant streams, durable retry waterfall, and structured terminal reasons are canonical.
seams.breakage: The old projection would misinterpret or miss new events and cannot invent RunId semantics.
seams.migration: Define an explicit new-event-to-RunId projection adapter and replay fixtures before integrating policy.

seams.oldContract: Custom policy observed provider errors, request attempts, reasoning, usage, and streams through older hooks.
seams.newContract: LlmFailure, LlmAttemptId, reasoningEffort capabilities, disjoint usage fields, transient streams, and provider-owned retry are explicit.
seams.breakage: Old error/retry and reasoning adapters would duplicate or conflict with provider behavior.
seams.migration: Reuse upstream facts/mechanism and add one DS Harness policy layer for IQ3_S and fatal evidence.

seams.oldContract: Custom durable events/projections targeted the older Session envelope.
seams.newContract: Session format v3, static migrations, generation/lease verification, known-event catalog, and ignorable unknown-event rules apply.
seams.breakage: Directly writing old custom envelopes can be rejected or make cross-version persistence unsafe.
seams.migration: Design TaskCheckpoint/Run durable facts for v3 and register or safely mark extension events according to upstream rules.

seams.oldContract: Custom pressure policy and compaction modified the old compaction-basic flow.
seams.newContract: Upstream owns token thresholds, atomic brackets, replacement generations, pruning, offload, and overflow recovery.
seams.breakage: Replaying the old engine would create two compaction systems and discard new safety behavior.
seams.migration: Keep upstream executor; add thin task-aware eligibility, low/medium scope, and deterministic fact validation.

seams.oldContract: A custom remote exposed Run State to RunStatusDock and closed the idle composer gap.
seams.newContract: Session controller transport, generated client APIs, scoped modules, and dockkit own current UI composition.
seams.breakage: RunStatusDock has no guaranteed matching insertion point or transport shape.
seams.migration: Rebuild transport and UI against current module/dock contracts after the Run projection is stable.

seams.oldContract: Electron 44, Node 24.17, node-pty, koffi, sharp, and fs-ext were qualified in the Custom package.
seams.newContract: Electron 44 remains; primary Node is 24.21, Python 3.12 is added, node-pty/koffi/sharp versions remain, and native/system N-API now owns locking while fs-ext is legacy-only.
seams.breakage: Old runtime smoke and copied binary assumptions omit Python/payload signatures and the new native/system boundary.
seams.migration: Use upstream runtime lock and add product-specific packaged ABI smoke after packaging is restored.

strategy.name: Fresh latest-upstream branch plus semantic capability port
strategy.rationale: All eleven registered seams changed, the histories diverge by 1548 upstream commits versus 12 baseline-only commits, and upstream now natively owns several foundations that old patches would duplicate.

rejected.A: Rebase would replay obsolete implementation assumptions across every changed seam and make conflict resolution look like semantic validation.
rejected.C: Full or broad cherry-pick preserves historical file-level patches rather than current capability contracts; only isolated commits may later be mined as evidence.
rejected.D: A hybrid integration strategy obscures the single source of truth. Selective source reuse is allowed inside strategy B, but the branch and architecture remain latest-upstream-first.

portOrder.goal: Reconfirm locked upstream health and toolchain
portOrder.stopGate: Target SHA or health classification differs without explanation.
Any path can collide with official Desktop or Stable DS Harness.

portOrder.goal: Profile, settings, sessions, and migration boundary
portOrder.stopGate: Any real-data path is touched or migration semantics remain unresolved.
Composition duplicates upstream-native services or cannot start isolated.

portOrder.goal: Session v3 and Agent lifecycle adapters
portOrder.stopGate: Run identity or durable-event compatibility is ambiguous.
decisions: D1 restore task/checkpoint and task/result-manifest as first-party known events instead of custom-event migration
D2 keep the old v1 schema and field names; RunId and AttemptId survive only as in-package compatibility identity types
D3 Stage 6 deliberately defines no logical RunId; that stays a Stage 7 decision
D4 LlmAttemptId remains transient and non-durable and is never persisted into a checkpoint
D5 two independent pure-library packages with no runtime companion and no composition entry
D6 no guarded and no pending-only resume; resume policy is deferred to Stage 8

portOrder.goal: Run State, backend health, and error classification
portOrder.stopGate: Unknown is guessed, fatal evidence is weak, or terminal state can regress.

portOrder.goal: TaskCheckpoint, Result Manifest, and guarded resume
portOrder.stopGate: Authoritative task facts can be lost or duplicated.

portOrder.goal: IQ3_S reasoning and bounded run policy
portOrder.stopGate: A second retry engine appears or request reasoning cannot be proven.
Compaction can mutate checkpoints, delete evidence, or lower main reasoning.
Diagnostics can mutate runtime or idle UI regresses.
Maintenance joins product runtime or changes cursor/debt.

portOrder.goal: Full isolated regression and candidate qualification
portOrder.stopGate: Any baseline invariant or safety sentinel fails; no install or new baseline.

safety.dataPlan: Use temporary DSH_HOME/userData/profile roots and copied synthetic/released fixtures only. Never point the adaptation build or migration code at the user's settings, sessions, profiles, or Application Support.
safety.nativePlan: Adopt the upstream primary-runtime lock, then verify architecture, payload hashes, codesign, Node/Python execution, native/system, node-pty, koffi, sharp, Host startup, and renderer loading in an isolated candidate.
safety.maintenancePlan: Port Phase 8B scripts late as a repository-only plane, adapt package/docs wiring, preserve cursor and scheduler state, and keep notifications material-change-only.

compatibilityDebt.reason: Stage 6 restored the two Final Product task events as first-party known v3 events and shipped the durable task-checkpoint contract plus a read-only lifecycle fact extractor, but Run State, retained capability ports, guarded resume, and a new product baseline remain unresolved.

knownUnknowns: Formal Developer ID/notarization and daily installation remain intentionally outside the isolated Stage 4 candidate qualification.
Run State still has no logical RunId: Stage 6 refused to define one, so Stage 7 must fix the turn/step/attempt-to-RunId projection contract before any policy layer consumes it.
Whether guarded and pending-only resume may proceed without a durable attempt identity, given that Stage 6 kept LlmAttemptId transient and non-durable, is a Stage 8 question.
The local IQ3_S route's final mapping into the current pi-ai model catalog must be proven without reading real settings in Stage 9.
The current dockkit/scoped-slot insertion contract for Run Details needs a minimal renderer prototype after its remote contract stabilizes.
Retained capability ports and current-client qualification remain unproven until their later stages.
